status: PROVISIONAL — every number here is our hypothesis for founder review, not Meta's. Meta publishes no budget per business size, niche or margin (docs/discovery-asesor-inversion-meta.md §11); it only gives the account's daily minimum (act_/minimum_budgets, always read live, never stored here) and «at least 7 days» to learn [S].
source: m-25091389. Anchor: the video Herwin shared — start at US$5 or US$10 a day depending on the size of the company (secondary source, not Meta's). Meta's old pricing page «start with at least $5», «at least seven days» [S, discovery §11]. Market-class modulation, size bands and pieces: Raul / backend, 2026-11-22, hypotheses.

business_size.source: hypothesis: the profile's «clientes nuevos que puedes atender por semana» (capacity) decides the size — < 20 = pequeno (anchor US$5/day), ≥ 20 = grande (anchor US$10/day). Without a profile we use pequeno («valores generales»). Not the monthly cap: the cap is already an upper bound, using it as the size too would count it twice. Not the rubro: Tu marca stores it as free text and there are no sourced numbers per rubro.

default_market_class_source: when Meta gave no audience range (no market estimate) we use the middle row

daily_minor.source: keys: currency → business size → market class (mercado-v1). USD = the anchor (US$5 small / US$10 larger business); a small market (< 50.000 people) gets less because it saturates sooner, a large market lets a small business go a bit above US$5. COP and UYU are the same dollars written in each currency at ~COP 4.000 and ~UYU 40 per US$ (rounded to $10.000 COP / $100 UYU), fixed here — never a live conversion. VES is absent on purpose: Venezuelan accounts run in USD (discovery §9).

days_source: Meta: «at least seven days, so our system has time to learn» [S, discovery §3 and §11]
pieces_source: hypothesis: one piece the first time (all the budget learns on it); with a previous promotion the suggested TOTAL is split across up to 3 pieces (discovery: one ad set with 2–3 ads; Raul 2026-11-22: split the total, never multiply it), fewer when a share would fall under Meta's daily minimum.
monthly_cap_source: code, not data: the suggested total never passes what is left of the profile's monthly cap this calendar month (cap − the brand's Insights spend this month); at most 30 days (UX 2026-11-22).
